# Small business resources

Biz Connect helps Alberta entrepreneurs find the tools, guidance and resources needed to launch and grow a successful business.

[Skip to On this page](https://www.alberta.ca/small-business-resources#on-this-page)

If your business is impacted by tariffs, find [tariff-related resources](https://www.alberta.ca/tariff-related-resources-for-alberta-businesses "Tariff-related resources for Alberta businesses") to help you navigate evolving trade challenges.

## Overview

Whether you are launching a new business or expanding an existing one, this page offers valuable information on business guidance, mentorship, training, permits and financing. Government initiatives like Biz Connect help Alberta small business owners overcome challenges, navigate regulations and access community and government supports tailored to diverse industries and needs. Explore this resource hub to discover practical solutions for sustainable business growth in Alberta’s competitive business landscape.

## Disasters and emergencies

### Natural disaster support

Businesses affected by natural disasters can contact [Business Link Alberta for free support](https://www.alberta.ca/small-business-resources#contact). Businesses can also contact [Biz Connect](https://www.alberta.ca/small-business-resources#contact) for referral to Alberta government business supports and programs.

### Emergency planning

Alberta offers the [Emergency response planning occupational health and safety tool kit](https://ohs-pubstore.labour.alberta.ca/bp040) to provide you with a step-by-step guide for ensuring your worksite is safe with specific contingencies in place in case of an emergency.

You can also contact your [local Chamber of Commerce](https://www.abchamber.ca/) for advice on emergency business planning.

## Start your business

### Advice, coaching and mentoring

[Business Link Alberta](https://businesslink.ca/) is a government supported organization that provides new and prospective small businesses with one-to-one guidance, practical business resources and market research. Business Link Alberta also connects small businesses to programs, funding and networks to help them start and grow their business ideas with confidence. 

*   ### Registering and licensing
    
    All businesses in Alberta must be registered in the province to conduct business.
    
    To get started, learn about structuring and registering your business, connect with a [Business Link Alberta](https://businesslink.ca/contact/) strategist.
    
    #### Structure and license your business
    
    Before registering your business, learn about business legal structures and which type might be right for you. [BizPal](https://services.bizpal-perle.ca/?b=48&lang=en) is a support tool that helps entrepreneurs and small businesses find permits and licences they may require when starting or managing a business.
    
    For more tips on licensing a business, contact your municipality's business licensing and permits service.
    
    #### Register your business
    
    Once you decide what kind of organization you would like to incorporate, learn about the step-by-step process for registration.
    
    #### Register an out-of-province business
    
    If you have a business that is active but not registered in Alberta, be sure to register your corporation with [Alberta’s Online Extra-provincial Registration](https://newwestregistration.alberta.ca/).
    
*   ### Funding
    
    [Futurpreneur](https://futurpreneur.ca/en/) offers loans of up to $75,000, mentoring and advice to entrepreneurs ages 18 to 39.
    
    [Community Futures](https://albertacf.com/) offers loans to rural businesses, and has 27 offices throughout Alberta.
    
    [ATB Entrepreneur Centre](https://atbentrepreneurcentre.com/) can help you find additional resources through funding, advice and connections to help you get started on your way or expand your business.
    
    Discover potential financing options through Alberta’s [Superintendent of Financial Institutions](https://www.alberta.ca/about-financial-institutions-news-links "Financial institutions – Overview"). It includes the regulatory framework surrounding capital lending and lists of accredited institutions.
    
    Alberta offers an [Innovation Employment Grant](https://www.alberta.ca/innovation-employment-grant "Innovation Employment Grant") for organizations of any size to conduct research and development. This program is designed to work in tandem with the Job Creation Tax Cut and can provide you with up 20% toward qualifying research and development expenditures.
    
    If your business requires employees to undergo specific training, the [Canada-Alberta Productivity Grant](https://www.alberta.ca/canada-alberta-productivity-grant "Canada-Alberta Productivity Grant") can provide assistance to cover 50% of costs up to $5,000 for an existing employee, or 75% of costs up to $10,000 for unemployed Albertans. This employer-driven program, which replaces the Canada-Alberta Job Grant, reimburses part of the training expenses to boost productivity and workforce competitiveness. Employers apply on behalf of their employees.
    
    [Alberta Innovates funding programs](https://albertainnovates.ca/funding/) help drive your innovative and technological ideas forward. They provide funding and support for small and medium-sized enterprises that are focused on addressing provincial challenges and benefitting Albertans.
    
    The [Agriculture Financial Services Corporation](https://afsc.ca/) is a provincial Crown corporation providing farm and commercial loans, in addition to hail, crop and livestock price insurance and farm income disaster insurance.
    
    The [Canada Small Business Financing Program](http://www.ic.gc.ca/eic/site/csbfp-pfpec.nsf/eng/Home) is a loan-sharing program between the Government of Canada and financial institutions which helps small businesses access financing of up to $1 million.
    
    Visit the [Business Development Bank of Canada](https://www.bdc.ca/en/financing) (BDC) to explore loans for businesses that have been active for at least 12 months. BDC also provides referrals for businesses that have been active for less than 12 months.
    
    The [Alberta Manufacturing Productivity Grant](https://www.alberta.ca/alberta-manufacturing-productivity-grant "Alberta Manufacturing Productivity Grant") provides up to $30,000 in matching funding to support small and medium-sized manufacturers across any sector looking to improve productivity and competitiveness.
